family.description: This family includes YjbQ from Escherichia coli, its orthologue from Pyrococcus furiosus and similar sequences. These proteins have been shown to have sufficient thiamine phosphate synthase activity to complement thiE mutants. However, it is presumed that this is a secondary activity, and the primary function of the YjbQ family enzyme remains unknown [[cite:PUB00101019],[cite:PUB00101020]].

edges.mechanism: The primary abstract reports that expression of the selected E. coli gene complements loss of thiE. Accessible Introduction identifies MC1061 delta-thiE. This is retained as an indirect cellular effect, not a measured catalytic microstep or constitutive thiamine pathway.

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The K12 reference P0AF48 sequenceversion1 is138 aa and exactly matches NP_418480.1, AAC77026.1, BAE78058.1 and WP_000270375.1. Reported in-vitro TPS activity, directed evolution and residue tests need full-text assay review before mechanistic edges are added. Rescue does not establish the native physiological role or justify transferring ThiE chemistry to YjbQ. Other-species complementation constructs remain unmapped.

edges.mechanism: YjbQ expression supports the TableII +++ colony phenotype in a host that does not grow on M9/glucose at37 C without rescue. The intervening reaction sequence and actual YjbQ substrate are unresolved; no direct PLP or OHPB production was measured for this edge.

edges.subject: express-yjbq

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Whole E. coli K12 YjbQ b4056/JW4017 corresponds to P0AF48/NP_418480.1 reference138 aa with PF01894 at6-138. Both expression systems add N-terminal His6; ASKA also adds five C-terminal residues. TableV printed pTrcHisB and pET45b forward primers differ in the YjbQ start region. The reference sequence match does not independently establish the experimental insert sequence or isolated-domain sufficiency.
causal_graphs.limitations: TablesII/SIII +++ means1 mm colonies after3-5 days, not a directly measured specific growth rate or20% catalytic activity. pdxB complementation is faster at1-2 days. FigureS1 labels YjbQ at4 days and vector at7 days, not matched-time growth rates. Failure to rescue separate serC,pdxA,pdxJ,pdxH mutants bounds the effect but is not a matched double-knockout causal chain. Proposed OHPB entry is inferred; YjbQ dehydrogenase activity was not assayed because soluble protein was unavailable. JU283 was selected from heterogeneous Keio stocks for its30 C phenotype; transfer to all delta-pdxB isolates is not established.

record.description: This family includes YjbQ from Escherichia coli, its orthologue from Pyrococcus furiosus and similar sequences. These proteins have been shown to have sufficient thiamine phosphate synthase activity to complement thiE mutants. However, it is presumed that this is a secondary activity, and the primary function of the YjbQ family enzyme remains unknown [[cite:PUB00101019],[cite:PUB00101020]].

evidence.explanation: The primary report supports qualitative thiE rescue and reports biochemical/mutagenesis work; full figures, exact conditions, active-site assignments and other-species constructs remain uninspected.

TableII, supplementary TableIII and Results support genotype/context-specific growth. Supplementary purification Methods confirms insoluble YjbQ. Original Figure1 marks the pathway2 precursor unknown; no measured OHPB-production or catalytic microstep is shown for YjbQ.

discussions.notes: Obtain readable2008 full text, resolve the2010 printed primer and FigureS1 antibiotic discrepancies, verify actual insert sequences and liquid-growth conditions, and assess purified products and residue controls. The2010 publisher supplement was obtained after the initial CREATE event. Do not convert an unperformed assay or unavailable source into negative evidence. Native physiological function and transfer across14125 frozen family proteins remain open.
discussions.prompt: Resolve YjbQ reactions while preserving the distinction between growth rescue and direct biochemical evidence.
discussions.rationale: Thiamine and vitamin B6 rescue occur in different hosts and pathways. Morett reports in-vitro TPS and mutagenesis, but full assay evidence was not obtained. Kim's proposed pathway2 entry is genetic inference and YjbQ was not assayed for4PE dehydrogenase activity; the broad statement that none of the selected proteins has this activity cannot be used as a measured YjbQ negative.

evidence.explanation: RhiN-related Results and Discussion explicitly leave its function unresolved; RhiG aldolase data and whole-cluster production do not establish individual RhiN chemistry.
The YjbQ-related selection rationale cites Morett2008 and removes thiE/yjbQ. The discussed ThiN H95 residue is not a YjbQ catalytic residue.
The inspected134-residue ST2072 deposition contains Zn/sulfate and a trimeric assembly; the2005 full paper and a residue-level functional assay were not reviewed.

discussions.notes: Identity comparisons, source-access outcomes and searched aliases are retained under evidence/PF01894. No frozen identity/counter changes, independent expert endorsement, full-family completion or publication are claimed.
discussions.prompt: Distinguish structural and pathway-context leads from demonstrated PF01894 reactions.
discussions.rationale: RhiN homology and a proposed dehydration role do not establish its enzymatic reaction. The2024 tRNA-selection study cites the existing YjbQ bypass as a reason for double deletion, rather than supplying independent YjbQ replication. ST2072's Zn/sulfate structure does not prove the E. coli enzyme mechanism. Similar gene names must not merge unrelated proteins.
